facts.fact: A HISP evaluation that visited 5 health zones in Kinshasa and Haut-Katanga in the last quarter of 2021 states that facilities send their reports on paper to the health zone office, where they are entered into the SNIS, the national DHIS2 platform; decentralised entry exists in some large facilities with reliable power and internet, but most entry is done centrally in the health zones and most facilities have no access to the platform.

The HISP evaluation of late 2021 states that MEASURE Evaluation had funded laptops and monthly internet fees for facility-based data entry in 63 health facilities in Kikula and Kapolowe, which worked for about two years until the project's recent closure, after which the funding stopped and the devices deteriorated without replacement or maintenance; the closure is not dated beyond 'recent'.

The HISP evaluation of late 2021 places the national DHIS2-based HMIS, in place at national scale since 2013, with the HMIS division of the Ministry of Health, which it says faces fluctuating funding and organisational fragmentation, and names Gavi, the Global Fund, USAID, CDC and MEASURE Evaluation as supporting partners alongside the government.

systems.owner: HMIS division of the Ministry of Health, with HISP and donor partners
systems.tiers: national scale since 2013; data entered at health zone offices (519 zones, 26 provinces) from facilities' paper reports; entry in some large facilities; used at zonal, provincial and national levels
